text: Ahead, the ordinary noise of Uruk continued—merchants, animals, arguments that had nothing to do with lids or locked drawers or the kind of debts that collected themselves.

speaker: Narrator

text: Three hundred cubits of mud-brick curtain wall, two collapsed towers, and a stretch of foundation that had been patched so many times the original line was anybody's guess. The temple clerk who hired them wanted measurements, load assessments, and a written recommendation on whether the whole section needed tearing down before the next flood season. Nothing shifted. Nothing breathed cooler air. Nothing carried notches.
speaker: Narrator

text: It was the most restful work they had done in weeks.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag walked the foundation with a measuring rod and a piece of chalk, marking every place the brick had settled more than a finger's width. Enhedu counted and sorted the reusable stone the way other people counted coin. Ninsun copied the older survey marks still visible on the inner face—temple codes, old ownership seals, the usual bureaucratic scars. Zik checked the places where later repairs had been cut into earlier ones, reading the sequence the way his father had taught him to read mortar.
